lots.what_it_is: Framed and matted hand-coloured engraved map, 'A Map of Van Diemen's Land including part of New South Wales from the best Authorities, 1822', W. Balch, Newington Butts, London
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher found no priced entries and my own web searches were refused (shared search budget used up), so there is no market evidence at all for this map. No currency rate used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Buyer's premium would be 19.8% (all-in = hammer x 1.198). Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Title, date and imprint were read from the photo, but there is no price evidence whatsoever and originality (engraving vs later facsimile) cannot be judged from one photo through glass.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crops: cartouche reads 'A Map of Van Diemen's Land, Including part of New South Wales. from the best Authorities. 1822.' with a 'REMARKS' text panel below (Tasman 1642 discovery, Hobart Town, settlement). Imprint under the neat line reads approximately 'Printed & Published as the Act directs ... by W. Balch, Newington Butts London, and J. Phillips(?) 47 Paternoster Row'. Longitude scale along the bottom, compass rose, New Holland and Bass's Strait lettered, hand colour on Tasmania and the NSW coast. Wooden frame with gilt slip and cream mat, glazed. No plate mark visible because the mat covers the margins.
lots.condition: Appears clean with even toning under glass; colour looks fresh. Margins, plate mark and paper hidden by the mat, so foxing, trimming or a reproduction cannot be ruled out.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you check whether this is an original 1822 engraving rather than a printed facsimile: is there a visible plate mark or chain lines in the paper if the back is opened, does the engraved line look raised under a loupe (versus a dot screen), and are there any labels on the backing board?
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (the researcher supplied no entries).
lots.score_reason: An original 1822 Balch map of Van Diemen's Land is an early Tasmanian printed map with local appeal and could be worth several hundred dollars, but I have no verified price to back that, and a framed facsimile would be worth little. Scored mid-range to reflect real upside discounted heavily for no evidence and authenticity risk.
lots.research_notes: WebSearch refused all three queries I tried (shared 200-per-turn budget used up). I did not work around the limit. A follow-up search (Invaluable, Gowans/Colville past results, Australian antique map dealers) is needed before bidding.

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For context only: new kettle retail AUD 274; Gowans all-in = hammer x 1.198.
lots.confidence_reason: The ALESSI INOX 18/10 ITALY base mark is read clearly and the shape matches the Graves 9093, but evidence is a single new-retail asking price.
lots.key_photo_findings: Base stamp reads 'ALESSI / INOX 18/10 / ITALY' (photo 4). Kettle: conical body with rivet-dot band, black ball finial, blue handle with red beads. The whistle on the spout is a pale green dragon, not the usual bird; a separate burgundy/red bird whistle lies loose in the box, so possibly two whistles or a mismatched one. Also a creamer and a lidded sugar bowl in the same design (photo 3), and a partial view of another domed piece at lower left. Kettle interior (photo 2) shows brown staining and scale on the base.
lots.condition: Used. Blue handle faded and slightly chalky, light scratches to the body and heavy scratching on the base, interior staining and scale in the kettle. Whistles look intact but the dragon may not be original to this kettle.
lots.question_for_gowans: Which pieces are in the lot (kettle, creamer, sugar bowl, any spoon or teapot), are both whistles included, and are there any dents or a cracked handle? Do the creamer and sugar bowl carry the Alessi mark?
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (the researcher supplied no entries). The scan-note guesses ($100-200 kettle, $150-250 set) are not evidence and were ignored.
lots.score_reason: Genuine Alessi Graves kettle with matching creamer and sugar bowl; used sets usually trade for a fraction of the AUD 274 new kettle price, so likely about AUD 80 to 180 for the lot, discounted for wear and only asking evidence.
